testsuite.name: com.chromascape.web.aiplayer.prototype.FishingShadowDecisionWriterTest

testcase.name: concurrent stop calls do not overlap shutdown processing
snapshot invariants hold during repeated concurrent writes
the writer status snapshot exposes lifecycle, queue, and counters atomically
enqueue racing with stop is either accepted before DRAINING and written, or rejected
a drain that exceeds the timeout interrupts the writer and reports DRAIN_TIMEOUT
the persistence queue preserves decision order
queue saturation produces a visible queue-full error and drops only
a successful append increments written and completed
a persistence failure does not block or stop inference
the writer refuses unsafe paths at the persistence boundary and counts them as failed
an interrupted shutdown join performs a real second join and restores the flag
a successful write clears a recoverable write failure
the writer rejects enqueue before start with SHADOW_PERSISTENCE_STOPPED
null decisions are rejected without side effects
a runtime serialization failure is counted and the loop continues
a blocked writer remains DRAINING after both joins and STOPPED only on exit
accepted queued items become abandoned on a forced exit, and DRAIN_TIMEOUT survives
the writer rejects enqueue once draining has begun
the writer rejects enqueue after stop with SHADOW_PERSISTENCE_STOPPED
an unsafe shadow run id is counted as failed, never written
a failed append increments failed and completed, never written
no accepted item remains queued after a successful shutdown
a terminal drain-timeout error survives a later successful write completion
an unsafe persistence path increments failed and completed, never written
the writer exposes queue size, written count, and dropped count
unexpected writer-loop termination produces WRITER_FAILED and abandons the queue
a queue-full item increments dropped, not enqueued
history reads remain safe during repeated concurrent appends
the writer drains during normal shutdown
flush finishes when all accepted writes have either succeeded or failed
